I bring population-based HIV evidence and careful testing to AI tools for global health programs.

## Personal Value Proposition

::: vp
As an HIV epidemiology researcher building skills in AI and machine learning, I help global health programs adopt AI tools that are grounded in population-based evidence such as PHIA data. I design and test these tools for the safety, privacy, and neutrality that sensitive health topics require, so that they support the people they serve rather than put them at risk.
:::

## About Me

I am an HIV epidemiology researcher. My work uses data from the Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (PHIA) surveys in Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, and Zimbabwe to study HIV status non-disclosure: who does not share their HIV status, and why.

I am currently studying machine learning fundamentals in the AIML-500 course at Indiana Wesleyan University. My goal is to connect these two fields: to help HIV and global health programs use AI in ways that are evidence-based, respect privacy, and protect people in stigmatized situations.
